messages.text: Starting the cycle. The release train is held. Nothing goes out until I understand why the health check keeps failing a change that looks fine.
I am on the vaults page. Every card drops down when its small yield chart finally loads. Worst movement we have measured on that page.
The positions endpoint went slow overnight, but only for the unluckiest requests. Pulling traces before I guess at a cause.
An advisory landed on the library we decompress incoming traffic with. A tiny payload can make it ask for more memory than the machine has.
Advisories are usually not reachable from outside. I want to prove this one is before I ask anyone to move a release date.
The gap is always the same height. So the chart knows its size perfectly well, and we simply never told the layout.
Does that need an account, or can anyone on the internet reach it.
Anyone. Straight from the public edge, nothing required past the first frame. I finished proving it a minute ago.
So the ingest gateway comes out of the 2026.32.1 scope. Shipping it as it stands puts that path into production.
Out of scope then. The train is held anyway. Tell me the moment there is a patched build and I will put it back.
Two problems stacked now. Mine is a check that cries wolf, his is real. I would rather be blocked by his than by mine.
Every slow request touches the last day of activity. Anything older is fine. That narrows it a long way.
My fix is small and the page is visibly broken today. Is there a path to shipping this cycle, or do I plan for next week.
Plan for this week. But the queue does not move while the train is held, so being small does not help you here.
Found it. Those requests add up a full day of gains as they go, and there is no index behind the lookup that feeds them.
Two part fix. Hold the space for the chart before it exists, and give it a name so a screen reader can say what it shows.
The check holding us watches errors across one long window. A quiet stretch drags the average down and it refuses to promote.
It is not wrong about the number. It is wrong about what the number means. That is the harder kind of thing to argue with.
The patch is a one line version bump. Suspiciously easy. If this path is that exposed, I should look at what sits above it.
When things move again I want a slow rollout for the endpoint fix. It changes how the database reads and I would rather not guess.
Patched build is up for the compression problem. The size limit now comes from us instead of being trusted from the incoming frame.
The hold has one upside. Nothing is using the slow rollout lane while the train is parked, so it is yours. Take it now.
Taking it. A small share of traffic at the new read path, and I watch the slow end before anything else changes.
If the caller can lie about how big a message is, patching the library only moved the lie one step earlier.
Space is reserved, the chart has a name, and I lowered how much movement the page is allowed before the build fails.
The stricter limit will annoy someone in three weeks. It is also the only part of this that stops the problem coming back.
Replacing the single window check with two. A fast one for a sudden break, a slow one for a steady leak. Both must agree to stop a release.
The slow end moved, but not enough. The index fixed the lookup and now the work after it is the slow part. I measured the wrong half.
Second change. It was loading a whole day of rows to answer a question about a much smaller window. Bounding that now.
Twenty minutes of random input at the frame parser and nothing. Either it is solid or my inputs are too polite. Making them stranger.
Where does the check rework stand. I would rather hear about a problem now than at the end of the cycle.
Two thirds. It is written and I am replaying last month's incidents through it to see whether it would have caught them.
Slow end is down from four hundred milliseconds to about forty. There is still a wasted copy of every row that does not need to happen.
Found something. A twelve byte header can claim sixty five thousand bytes of payload, and the parser sets that aside before checking.
Does that drop the connection or the whole process.
The process. One malformed frame takes the relay down for everyone connected to it.
Second time today he has reopened something I had written off as closed. I should stop treating his areas as finished until he says so.
Relay core stays off this train until the claimed length is capped. The library patch does not help if the caller sets the number.
Agreed, it stays off. How long for the cap. Under an hour and I hold the train rather than split the release.
Under an hour. It is one comparison against the bytes actually present. Proving nothing gets past it is the slow part.
The two window check is merged as #2291. A release now stops only when both measures agree that something is genuinely wrong.
Mine is ready and sitting in the queue, which is sitting on you. Nothing else stands between it and going out.
You are first through when the train moves. I am starting the small share rollout of the held candidate now.
The cap is in and the random input has gone quiet on the shape that used to crash it in seconds. Quiet for ten minutes is not proof.
Submitted the endpoint work as three separate commits, so any one of them can be undone without disturbing the others.
The old check would have stopped this rollout twice already on quiet traffic. The new one has not flinched. That is the whole argument.
Reading yours. The smaller window quietly returns less data if a caller asks for more than a day. Is that written down anywhere.
It is not, and it should refuse instead of trimming. Better a caller sees an error than a total that looks right and is not.
Second time today I made something faster and slightly wrong. Faster and wrong is not a trade I am allowed to make.
The held candidate is at half traffic and both measures are quiet. If that holds, the train goes out and the queue starts moving.
I would like to say the way in is closed. What I can honestly say is that the two ways in I know about are closed.
The queue is frozen while the train is held, so the check on #2417 is parked behind my gate work. It is not your change failing.
I assumed it was mine and spent ten minutes rereading a two line change. Useful to know where the wait actually is.
Train is at full traffic and healthy. The queue is moving again and your check has been released.
It went green and is merged as #2417. The cards hold their shape from the first paint and the chart announces what it is.
Release train 2026.32.1 is promoted. Everything that was held goes out on it, including the gateway that came back into scope.
Relay fix is merged as #1183. The advisory and the crasher sitting above it are both closed on that path.
Endpoint work is up as #1487. Faster, bounded, and it now refuses a question it cannot answer honestly.
The tighter limit will fail someone's build next week and they will ask me to raise it. I should write down now why the answer is no.
One more on yours. There is an error budget advisory open until 2026.32.2, so your migration rides that train. I will book the window.
That is fair. I would rather it ran on a quiet morning with someone watching than at the tail end of a release day.
Cycle is closed. One train out, one migration waiting for the next, and nothing in production that we know to be wrong.
